title: Deep learning assesses heart allograft rejection from biopsy whole-slide images
summary: A deep learning system analysing gigapixel endomyocardial biopsy slides detected allograft rejection with an AUC of 0.962, distinguished cellular and antibody-mediated rejection (AUCs 0.958 and 0.874) and graded rejection with an AUC of 0.833. In a human reader study it was non-inferior to conventional assessment and reduced interobserver variability and assessment time. Caveat: test cohorts from the US, Turkey and Switzerland are retrospective and the authors call for clinical trials.
ai_technology: Deep learning on whole-slide images for endomyocardial biopsies
organization: Harvard Medical School; Ege University; Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; University of California San Diego

evidence.tested: Rejection detection (AUC 0.962) was measured on a curated US dataset and independent test cohorts from Turkey and Switzerland, and a human reader study found the system non-inferior to conventional assessment.
evidence.unknown: The authors state that clinical trials are needed to establish the efficacy of AI-assisted biopsy assessment.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning system analysed gigapixel endomyocardial biopsy whole-slide images to detect, subtype and grade rejection.
